items.content_html:
Value Prop

We're making it easier to land changes by enabling you to break up the changes into separate pull requests that are stacked on top of each other. Each pull request in the stack is aware of the other pull requests in the stack and what its ultimate target branch is (so the appropriate branch protections and rules are enforced) and individual parts (or the entire stack) can be merged as soon as they are ready.

Because each part of the stack is a just a pull request, there is a low barrier to entry, does not require major changes to your team's workflows, and works with existing apps and tools.

Expected Outcome

  1. Pull requests can be stacked on top of each other, with the appropriate branch protections and rules applied on each pull request in the stack.
  2. All or part of the stack can be merged once the necessary requirements have been met.
  3. Works with existing app and tools that understand branches and pull requests.
items.title: Pull request stacks [Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

The Code Security Risk Assessment will complement the existing Secret Risk Assessment to scan your organization for security vulnerabilities. The Code Security Risk Assessment will deliver a consolidated report highlighting both vulnerabilities so your businesses can quickly prioritize remediation.

Expected Outcome

GitHub is committed to helping organizations strengthen their security posture by making it easier to identify and address security risk in code. The Code Security Risk Assessment helps you understand your organization’s security posture and risk exposure, so you can determine where to enable security tooling to better protect your code.
items.title: On-demand Code Security Risk Assessment

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Customers appreciate the way composite actions enable them to easily take multiple steps and repeat them easily in jobs. However, they also wish to split out the steps within the job rather than keeping it within the composite action. This increases readability and makes it easy for users to analyze individual steps.

Expected Outcome

Enable composite actions to split out their steps within a job, rather than being treated as a single composite entity.
items.title: Action supports splitting out composite Action steps [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Environments auto-deploy when added to Actions workflows. This is useful, but also a pain point if you only want to use the environment's variables, not deploy to it. Using environments to store secrets and bind them to a branch is a huge security win, but for others it's more about usability and avoiding deployment spam on a pull request.[/+]

Expected Outcome

With this release, developers can now use environments without them auto-deploying them. This will be accomplished by adding a boolean option in Actions workflows to note if deployment is true or false.
items.title: Actions now allows developers to use environments without auto-deployment [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Customers want to be able to control how their work is executed when the number of workflows or jobs exceed what they are able to process in a given time period.

Expected Outcome

We will be adding clear concepts of both concurrency limits, concurrency queues (for jobs/workflows that haven't run but exceed the concurrency), and processes for queueing/dequeueing.
items.title: Actions improved job and workflow concurrency [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

This feature gives users clear, at-a-glance visibility into agent activity directly within GitHub Projects, so they always know what’s in progress and where work is happening. By surfacing agent status on issues and enabling quick navigation to active sessions, teams can manage agent and human work together without leaving their planning workflow.

Expected Outcome

Teams should be able to plan, review, and coordinate work more efficiently, especially as they scale to multiple and third-party agents within a single project.
items.title: Agent awareness on GitHub Projects [Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Today, once an issue is assigned to an agent, there’s no visibility into whether work is in progress or complete without navigating to a PR or session. This update surfaces agent status directly on issues, giving users at-a-glance insight into progress so they know when to review work and can manage agent and human effort in one place. As support for third-party agents expands, this visibility also makes it easier to track and coordinate multiple agent sessions directly from the issue.

Expected Outcome

Improve transparency and coordination by making agent work visible where teams already plan and track work. This helps users confidently understand progress, reduce context switching, and better coordinate agent and human contributions.
items.title: Agent issue assignment progress and session management [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Code Quality gives you advanced quality checks such as maintainability, reliability, and overall code health. This delivers a single, seamless workflow for teams to improve code quality and reduce technical debt, directly within GitHub.

Expected Outcome

With GitHub Code Quality enabled, customers can expect to catch and address a broader range of code issues earlier in the development process. This results in cleaner, more reliable code, less time spent on rework, and a stronger competitive position as teams build high-quality software faster and more confidently.
items.title: GitHub Code Quality [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

The GitHub Code Quality Organization-level Quality Dashboard gives engineering leaders and administrators a big-picture view of code quality across all repositories in their organization. The dashboard surfaces key metrics, making it easier to assess, compare, and improve code health at scale.

Expected Outcome

With this dashboard, organizations can quickly identify areas of high or low quality and prioritize technical debt across teams. Viewing code quality at the organization level leads to more informed decision making and more focused engineering investments.
items.title: GitHub Code Quality: Organization-level Quality Dashboard [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Code Quality Organization-level Enablement gives administration teams an efficient way to activate Code Quality features across multiple repositories at once. By providing a centralized workflow, it simplifies setup, ensures consistency, and accelerates adoption of code quality tools throughout the organization.

Expected Outcome

With this feature, organizations can expect faster onboarding of Code Quality on many repos, reducing manual effort and helping teams achieve improved code standards more quickly. Administrators spend less time on individual configurations, empowering all teams to benefit from better code hygiene right away.
items.title: GitHub Code Quality: Organization-level Enablement

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Code Quality REST APIs enable organizations to programmatically access and manage Code Quality features that were previously only available through the UI. This gives customers the flexibility to automate workflows, integrate with internal tools, and scale code quality processes to fit their unique environments.

Expected Outcome

With the introduction of Code Quality REST APIs, customers can streamline their code quality management and set up custom automations across repositories and teams. This results in more efficient, scalable, and tailored code governance, helping organizations improve software quality while saving time.
items.title: GitHub Code Quality: REST APIs [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Code Quality Enterprise Policy empowers organizations with control over the availability of Code Quality at the enterprise level. By separating Code Quality from Code Security policy management, enterprises can confidently enable Code Quality functionality for their teams without risk of incurring Code Security-related costs.

Expected Outcome

With the new Code Quality enterprise policy, administrators can provide developers access to code quality insights while maintaining strict control over security settings and spend. This separation helps organizations manage adoption based on their needs and ensures compliance with internal governance and budgeting requirements.
items.title: GitHub Code Quality: Enterprise Policy [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Users can now assign code scanning alerts—individually or within a security campaign—to an agentic version of Autofix that autonomously creates pull requests to fix the problem. Unlike the current Autofix, this agentic version uses tool calling and advanced agent behaviors to iteratively test, validate, and refine fixes before presenting them to developers.

This release covers the initial public preview, focused on campaigns and individual alerts. A separate GA release will follow.

Expected Outcome

  • Increased rate of security alert remediation across customer organizations
  • Higher Autofix acceptance rates compared to current non-agentic version
  • Reduced time from alert creation to merged fix
  • Decreased manual effort spent on security debt reduction initiatives
items.title: Agentic autofix generation for code scanning alerts [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

When Sentry pinpoints the root cause of an error, you shouldn’t have to stop and switch tools to get it fixed. This feature lets you launch the Copilot coding agent straight from Sentry Root Cause Analysis (Seer), automatically carrying over the right context so you can go from insight to action in a single click.

Expected Outcome

Faster fixes with less friction. Instead of copying stack traces, hunting down the right files, and re-explaining the problem in GitHub, you can generate a strong first pass at the code change immediately and move straight into review. The result: shorter time-to-fix for Sentry issues, smoother on-call and triage workflows, and more time spent shipping improvements, not stitching together context across tools.
items.title: Launch Copilot coding agent from Sentry Root Cause Analysis

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Many engineering teams live in Jira to plan, triage, and assign work, yet they have to leave Jira to actually kick off implementation with Copilot coding agent. This release brings Copilot coding agent into Jira, so you can assign our coding agent to a Jira work item (from the assignee dropdown or via @mention) and let it start working with the right task context.

Expected Outcome

Less friction between planning and shipping. Teams can delegate well scoped coding tasks to Copilot directly from Jira, and still keep code review and merging in GitHub. The result can lead to a smoother workflow for Jira centric teams and faster progress from “assigned” to “PR ready for review”.
items.title: GitHub Copilot for Jira: Pubic Preview

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Copilot intelligently routes requests to the best model for a developer's specific task, allowing them to benefit from improved service reliability and less rate limiting, all without the cognitive load of model selection. Auto continues to align with model policies and provides discounted model rates for paid plans, providing cost optimization alongside performance.

Expected Outcome

Developers get faster, more relevant results without needing to choose models manually, increasing productivity and consistency across use cases. Organizations benefit from simplified adoption, improved experience at scale, and clearer value realization through smart, cost-aware routing.
items.title: A more intelligent Copilot auto model selection, optimizing for your task

items.content_html:
Value Prop

On March 1, 2026 the $0.002 per-minute Actions cloud platform charge will begin applying to self-hosted runner usage in private repositories.

This will not impact Actions usage in public repositories or GitHub Enterprise Server customers.

Expected Outcome

This aligns pricing to match consumption patterns, ensuring consistent service quality across hosting modalities as usage grows. This will result in significant improvements to our self-hosted offering, including the following releases over the coming year:

GitHub Scale Set Client

This new client provides enterprises with a lightweight Go SDK to build custom autoscaling solutions without the complexity of Kubernetes or reliance on ARC. It integrates seamlessly with existing infrastructure—containers, virtual machines, cloud instances, or bare metal—while managing job queuing, secure configuration, and intelligent scaling logic. Customers gain a supported path to implement flexible autoscaling, reduce setup friction, and extend GitHub Actions beyond workflows to scenarios such as self-hosted Dependabot and custom automation agents.

Multi-Label Support

We are reintroducing multi-label functionality for both GitHub-hosted larger runners and self-hosted runners, including those managed by Actions Runner Controller (ARC) and the new Scale Set Client.

Actions Runner Controller 0.14.0

This release introduces major quality-of-life improvements, including refined Helm charts for easier Docker configuration, enhanced logging, updated metrics, and formalized versioning requirements. It also announces the deprecation of legacy ARC, providing a clear migration path to a more reliable and maintainable architecture. Customers benefit from simplified setup, improved observability, and confidence in long-term support, reducing operational friction and improving scalability.

Actions Data Stream

Actions Data Stream will deliver a real-time, authoritative feed of GitHub Actions workflow and job event data, including metadata such as action versions. This capability enhances observability and troubleshooting by enabling organizations to integrate event data into monitoring and analytics systems for compliance and operational insights. By providing structured, high-fidelity data at scale, it eliminates reliance on manual log parsing and empowers teams to proactively manage reliability and performance.
items.title: GitHub Actions new pricing - Self-hosted runner price increase

items.content_html:
Value Prop

On January 1, 2026, GitHub will reduce the price of GitHub-hosted runners by up to 39%. The free usage minute quotas will remain the same.

This reduction is driven by a price reduction of base rates on all runners, paired with a new $0.002 per-minute GitHub Actions cloud platform charge. For GitHub-hosted runners, the new Actions cloud platform charge is already included in the reduced meter price.

Usage of standard GitHub-hosted runners in public repositories will remain free.

Expected Outcome

This price reduction makes high-performance compute more accessible for both high-volume CI workloads and the agent jobs that rely on fast, secure execution environments.

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Multi-label support in Actions Runner Controller (ARC) gives enterprises the flexibility to manage complex workflows without duplicating infrastructure. Instead of maintaining separate scale sets for each configuration, customers can assign multiple labels. For example a single scale set could have labels that represent attributes for operating system, hardware, compliance, and network configuration. This capability simplifies runner management, reduces operational overhead, and ensures jobs land on the right compute resources with minimal effort.

Expected Outcome

Customers gain a streamlined approach to autoscaling and job routing, improving resource utilization and reducing idle capacity. This results in lower infrastructure costs, faster execution, and better alignment with compliance and performance requirements, delivering an efficient and scalable self-hosted runner experience.
items.title: Multi-Label Support for Actions Runner Controller (ARC)

items.content_html:
Value Prop

ARC 0.14.0 delivers a more streamlined and reliable experience for managing self-hosted runners at scale. With refined Helm charts for easier Docker configuration, improved logging for faster troubleshooting, updated metrics aligned with platform availability initiatives, and formalized versioning requirements, this release reduces operational complexity and enhances observability. It also introduces a clear migration path by announcing legacy ARC deprecation, ensuring customers can transition to a more robust and maintainable architecture.

Expected Outcome

Customers benefit from simplified configuration, better visibility into runner health, and improved reliability across their environments. These enhancements reduce friction during setup and maintenance, minimize downtime through clearer metrics and logging, and provide confidence in long-term support through structured versioning. By moving away from legacy ARC, organizations gain a modern foundation that supports scalability and future innovation, creating a more predictable and efficient experience for platform teams.
items.title: Actions Runner Controller Release 0.14.0
